first30Days.title: Your first 30 days
first30Days.lead: The order here isn't arbitrary. Each step unlocks the next, and doing them out of order costs you weeks for no reason.

sections.p: American paperwork is chained together. The bank wants an address, the licence wants a Social Security number, and work apps want a bank account. Start at the wrong end and you go in circles. This order breaks the circle.

This is the first and most important document. Without it there's no formal work and, in most states, no licence. If you requested it on your DS-260 it usually arrives by post without you doing anything. If you didn't, you can go to a Social Security office yourself.
list: Go early — a delay here delays everything after it
Take your passport and visa
The card arrives by post, so you need a stable address first

sections.p: The cheapest and fastest thing, and everything after it asks for one. Prepaid lines don't need credit history or a contract.
list: Most prepaid lines don't require an SSN
This number becomes your contact on every application you make

sections.p: Some banks open an account with just a passport and visa; others want an SSN. Ask at two branches before deciding.
list: Ask about monthly fees and minimum balances — these quietly eat money
Bring proof of address if you have it

sections.p: Even if you haven't settled, you need somewhere that receives your post. Post isn't optional here — official cards and letters arrive that way.
list: A friend's address or where you're staying works temporarily
When you move, forward your post officially

sections.p: Even if you won't drive soon, a state ID makes everything easier because it's accepted identification everywhere. Licence procedures and requirements vary by state — see the state comparison page.
list: Some states have a waiting period after you arrive
Ask whether the test is available in your language

sections.p: Buying a car, long-term subscriptions, and any 12-month contract. In your first month you don't yet know where you'll settle or what you'll do — a long commitment now closes off your options.

first30Days.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

housing.title: Your first home
housing.lead: The hard part isn't the price — it's convincing someone to rent to you when you have no history in the country.

sections.p: Management companies look at your credit and rental history, and you have neither yet. This isn't personal rejection — the system simply can't see you. The answer isn't to fight the system, it's to come in through a different door.
Easiest and cheapest first:
list: A room in a shared flat with people already living there — fastest route, and the agreement is with them
Renting from an individual landlord rather than a management company — more flexible, and they'll actually listen
A short-term rental for a month or two until you find work and know where to settle
Offering several months upfront instead of credit history — but budget carefully, it eats into your early money

sections.p: Contracts here are enforced literally. Read it, and if something is unclear ask before signing, not after.
list: Lease length, how to break it early, and what that costs
Whether utilities are included
How much the deposit is and when it's returned
Guest and occupancy policy

sections.p: This is where newcomers get scammed most, and the signs are consistent:
list: Priced far below the market
The 'landlord' is abroad and you can't see the place before paying
Asks for a wire transfer or gift cards before any viewing
Rushes you and says others are waiting
Won't meet you or show you inside

sections.h: The one rule you never break
sections.p: Never pay anything before you've seen the place with your own eyes and seen a written lease. Anyone pressuring you to pay before that is running a scam, however right everything else looks.

housing.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

credit.title: Building credit from zero
credit.lead: A credit score is a number telling lenders whether you pay people back. You arrive with no number at all — not good, not bad, nothing.

sections.p: That number sets your car loan rate, sometimes your car insurance, and whether flats accept you. The gap between thin credit and good credit is measured in thousands of dollars on a single car loan. That's why it's worth starting in month one even if you don't need to borrow.
The usual path is simple, slow, and has no shortcut:
list: A secured credit card: you deposit money that becomes your limit — the bank takes no risk, so they accept you with no history
Use it for small regular expenses like fuel or your phone bill
Pay the balance **in full** every month, before the due date
Don't use more than a small share of your limit
Don't open several cards at once

sections.p: These do more damage than anything else: paying late even by a day, and using your whole limit every month. The score is built from consistency, not from amounts — a small card you pay exactly on time beats a large one you pay late.

sections.h: Never pay anyone to 'fix' your credit
sections.p: Nobody can build you a credit history for money. Companies promising this take your money and nothing else. History is built with time and consistency, and there is no substitute for that.

credit.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

health.title: Health insurance
health.lead: Care here is shockingly expensive. Having insurance isn't a luxury — one uninsured emergency visit can wipe out months of budget.

sections.p: As a permanent resident you have more than one route, and which fits depends on your income and your state. The two main paths are government coverage for lower incomes, and a marketplace where you buy a plan with subsidies based on income. Rules vary substantially by state, and some states extend coverage further than others.

The marketplace opens for a set period each year, but newly arriving in the country counts as a circumstance that opens a special enrolment window for you. So don't wait for the general period — ask as soon as you arrive.
list: Ask specifically about the special enrolment period for new arrivals
Estimate your likely subsidy with the take-home calculator

sections.p: This is where the biggest savings are. The emergency room is for genuinely serious cases and bills many times more. Urgent care handles the middle ground — bad colds, minor cuts, small fractures — at a fraction of the cost.
list: Chest pain, trouble breathing, heavy bleeding, major injury → emergency room
Fever, minor cut, infection, bad cough → urgent care

sections.p: Community health centres charge on a sliding scale based on income, and hospitals have financial assistance programmes. Ask about these **before** treatment, not after the bill arrives — they're completely different processes.

health.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

taxes.title: Your first year of taxes
taxes.lead: If you worked even one month, you probably owe a return. It's simpler than it looks, but ignoring it makes it bigger.

sections.p: This distinction changes everything. As an employee, the company withholds tax from your pay and gives you a W-2 at year end. Working delivery apps, you are legally self-employed: nobody withholds anything, and you're responsible for the whole amount — including self-employment tax, which is higher than people expect.

sections.h: Doing gig work? Set money aside from day one
sections.p: The most common trap for newcomers: earning well for months, spending all of it, then facing a tax bill at year end with nothing put by. Put a share of every payment into a separate account from the start.
list: Log your work mileage daily — that deduction is worth a lot
Keep receipts for work expenses
The gig calculator on this site shows the share you should be setting aside

sections.p: There are programmes that let you file for free below a certain income, and centres that help people in person for free — many offering help in several languages. Don't pay anyone to file a return you can file for nothing.
If your income is small and the process confuses you, that's not a reason to ignore it. Delay adds penalties, and filing is usually simpler than the fear of it.

taxes.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

credentials.title: Your qualifications and profession
credentials.lead: Your degree doesn't get cancelled at the border — but it isn't automatically accepted either. Credential evaluation and professional licensing are two different things.

sections.p: Specialised organisations take your qualification and issue a report saying what it's equivalent to in the US system. That's what most employers and universities ask for. It's not a government process — these are companies, with different prices and turnaround times, so compare before choosing.

Some professions can't legally be practised without a licence from the state itself: medicine, nursing, pharmacy, law, engineering, teaching and others. And licensing **varies by state** — which means choosing a city isn't only a cost-of-living decision, it's a career decision.
list: Find out early: does your profession need a licence in the state you're heading to?
These processes take months, sometimes years, and exams
Some professions have a shorter route for foreign-trained graduates

sections.p: The reality is licensing takes time and you need income now. Most people work something interim while moving through licensing in parallel. That isn't giving up — it's the sensible order.

sections.h: Something to do before you leave
sections.p: Get official copies of your certificates, transcripts and experience letters before you travel, with certified translations. Requesting these from abroad afterwards is far harder.

credentials.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

greenCard.title: Keeping your residency
greenCard.lead: A green card is permanent residence — but 'permanent' is conditional on actually living here.

sections.p: Your status as a permanent resident rests on the US being your actual home. Long or repeated absences can be read as abandoning residence, even while the card itself is still valid. The exact absence limits and conditions must be confirmed from the official source before any long trip.

sections.h: If you need to be away a long time
sections.p: There's a process you file **before** travelling that protects your status for longer. The important word is 'before' — travel first and try to fix it afterwards, and your options shrink sharply.
list: Ask about this process before you book
Keep anything proving your life is here: lease, work, tax return, bank account

sections.p: After a set period of residence you can apply for citizenship, and the requirements include a residence period, continuous presence, and a test. The exact periods come from the official authority — but what matters now is that long absences affect this too, so what you do in your first years matters later.

First: file a tax return every year even if your income is small — it's part of proving you live here. Second: report address changes within the required window; that's a formal obligation, not a detail.

greenCard.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

family.title: Family and children
family.lead: Children adapt far faster than you do. The hard part at first is the paperwork and the school.

sections.h: School is a right, not a privilege
sections.p: Public education is free and available to all resident children, regardless of their parents' status. Your school is determined by your home address — which is why choosing a neighbourhood is not a small detail when you have children.
It varies by district, but most ask for:
list: Proof of address (lease or utility bill)
The child's birth certificate
Immunisation records
A language assessment to place them in the right programme

sections.p: Schools require certain immunisations before starting. If you have your child's records from home, bring them translated — it avoids repeating vaccinations and saves time. Anything missing gets completed here.

sections.h: Language support exists and is free
sections.p: Schools run programmes for children whose first language isn't English, and this is the child's right, not an extra service. Ask for it by name at enrolment.

Children pick up the language fast and become the family's translator. That's convenient at first but puts a weight on them that isn't theirs — build your own language independence in parallel, however slowly.

family.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

carGuide.title: Buying a car from scratch
carGuide.lead: If your city needs a car, this is the biggest financial decision of your first year. Read this before walking into any dealership.

sections.h: First: do you even need one?
sections.p: Before anything else, check your city's car need on the city comparison page. If your city is one you can live in without a car, delaying a purchase by months saves thousands — the single biggest difference you can make to your first-year budget.

Without credit, the interest rate you're offered will be far higher than anyone else's. That's normal, not an exception. An $8,000 car can cost substantially more than that over the loan. The car calculator on this site shows you that gap in actual numbers.

sections.h: The title type — the most important word in the listing
sections.p: The title is the car's ownership document, and its condition is recorded on it:
list: clean — no major accident history. This is what you want
salvage — the car was written off as a total loss. Stay away
rebuilt / reconstructed — was salvage and was repaired. Much cheaper, much riskier, and insuring it is a problem
flood — water damage. The electrical faults appear later and never really go away

sections.p: A dealer costs more but has clearer paperwork and sometimes a short warranty. A private sale is cheaper but everything is on you: you check the paperwork, you arrange the inspection, and there's no going back after payment.

This is the step that separates a good car from a disaster. You take the car to a mechanic **you** chose — not one the seller recommended — and they inspect it for a small fee. Any seller who refuses this has answered your question.
list: Choose the mechanic yourself
Ask for a written report
If the seller refuses, walk away — whatever the price

sections.h: The true cost isn't the price
sections.p: The price is one part of the calculation. Add insurance (very expensive for a driver with no US driving history), registration, fuel and maintenance. Use the car calculator to see the real monthly figure, and compare it against renting one from an app.

sections.h: If someone rushes you, here's your answer
sections.p: There is no 'bargain that's about to go'. Urgency is the pressure tactic bad cars are sold with. A real bargain is one where the seller is willing to wait while you get it inspected.

carGuide.disclaimer: This site is not legal advice. It explains and organises; the official authorities are always the final word.

listingCheck.title: Car listing checker
listingCheck.lead: Paste a listing and we'll show you what should worry you in it.
listingCheck.localOnly: The check runs entirely on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
listingCheck.noFlags: No clear warning signs in the text. That doesn't mean the car is good — it still needs a mechanical inspection before you buy.

rules.dangerWords: ⛔ The listing contains words like salvage, rebuilt or as-is. These mean the car was written off or is sold with no guarantee at all. Not a first car.
rules.scamPattern: ⛔ The listing uses a known scam pattern: seller abroad, payment by gift card or wire, or 'shipping the car' to you. These aren't real ways of selling cars.
rules.tooLowMiles: ⚠️ The mileage is very low for the model year. Either the number has been tampered with, or the car sat unused for years — both are problems.
rules.tooHighMiles: ⚠️ The mileage is very high for the model year. Not automatically a no, but expect far more maintenance.
rules.suspiciouslyCheap: ⛔ The price is below any reasonable level. A price that's too good isn't a bargain — it's the most common scam bait.
rules.rushPressure: ⚠️ The listing is rushing you. Urgency is a pressure tactic, not a circumstance.
rules.noPrice: ⚠️ No clear price in the listing.

listingCheck.inspection: However clean the listing looks, never buy a used car without a mechanic you chose inspecting it before you pay. If the seller refuses that — walk away.
listingCheck.disclaimer: This tool only reads text. It is not a substitute for a mechanical inspection.
